questions.question: Where in the paper is the stated contribution established?
questions.quote: Our primary contribution is a formal proof that adaptive retrieval converges under bounded query drift.
questions.resolution: Either add the work that establishes it, or narrow the claim to what the paper actually shows. Narrowing is not a retreat, it is the difference between a claim you can defend and one you cannot.
questions.why: The paper claims a contribution that nothing in the body picks up: bounded, contribution, converges, drift, primary, proof, under. A reviewer checks the contribution against the results first, and a gap there is the most common single cause of rejection.

questions.question: Outperforms what, exactly?
questions.quote: Additionally, our method significantly outperforms all prior approaches and delivers the best results reported to date.
questions.resolution: Name the systems compared against and cite them, or say which configuration of your own method is the baseline.
questions.why: A comparison with no named point of comparison cannot be checked or reproduced. A reviewer who cannot tell what you beat has to assume you chose the comparison that flattered the result.

questions.question: What hyperparameters were used?
questions.resolution: State the hyperparameters in the method or in an appendix.
questions.why: The paper never states the hyperparameters. A reader cannot judge whether the result is solid or reproduce it without knowing, and a reviewer will ask rather than guess.

questions.question: How many runs was this averaged over, and how were seeds handled?
questions.resolution: State the number of runs in the method or in an appendix.
questions.why: The paper never states the number of runs. A reader cannot judge whether the result is solid or reproduce it without knowing, and a reviewer will ask rather than guess.

questions.question: What test supports "significantly" here?
questions.quote: Additionally, our method significantly outperforms all prior approaches and delivers the best results reported to date.
questions.resolution: Report the test and its outcome, or the effect size with an interval. If the difference was not tested, delete 'significantly' and state the measured difference instead.
questions.why: In a results section that word is read as a claim about statistical significance. With no test, effect size, or interval behind it, a reviewer cannot tell whether it means a measured result or an impression, and will assume the latter.

questions.question: What test supports "substantially" here?
questions.quote: This is a novel finding that substantially advances the field.
questions.resolution: Report the test and its outcome, or the effect size with an interval. If the difference was not tested, delete 'substantially' and state the measured difference instead.
questions.why: In a results section that word is read as a claim about statistical significance. With no test, effect size, or interval behind it, a reviewer cannot tell whether it means a measured result or an impression, and will assume the latter.

questions.question: Which part of the method produces the gain?
questions.resolution: Report the result with each component removed in turn, or state plainly that the components were not separated and why.
questions.why: A method with several components and no per-component evidence leaves a reviewer unable to tell what the contribution is. Whether this is required depends on the venue, and no verified profile was available for yours.
